newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean labour union body calls strike.
newsitem.headline: South Korean labour union body calls strike.

text.p: A militant South Korean union body on Thursday called an immediate strike of all its members in protest against the passage of a controversial labour law, a union official said.
The outlawed Korea Confederation of Trade Unions is the country's second largest union umbrella body and claims 500,000 members at leading export companies.
"We have called an immediate and indefinite strike," the official, Yoon Young-mo, said by telephone. "All members will stay away from their work sites and hold protest rallies across the country."
A spokeswoman for South Korea's largest union body, the Federation of Korean Trade Unions, said a decision on strike action would be taken at a meeting at 10.00 a.m. (0100 GMT).
At around dawn on Thursday the ruling New Korea Party rammed the labour law through the National Assembly with no opposition deputies present.
The hotly debated bill challenges decades of near-total job security in South Korea by giving employers the right to lay off workers and adopt flexible working hours.
